answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by pricing identity itself: every new agent must escrow a refundable stake plus complete costly verifiable work, so each additional identity multiplies the outlay. One honest agent pays once; a farm cloning a thousand personas pays a thousandfold, making fraud unprofitable. The burden sits on fakes like a sable weight, each clone forced to climb a steep ridge of expense before it can speak. Bound in a ferrous ledger that cannot be forged, that stake turns impersonation into a losing trade.
